title: Jak minął weekend?
text:
Ewa: Cześć, Michał! Jak minął weekend?
Michał: Dobrze, dzięki. W sobotę byłem z dziećmi na basenie, a w niedzielę pojechaliśmy do babci. A ty? Co robiłaś?
Ewa: W sobotę sprzątałam mieszkanie. W niedzielę rano pojechałam z mężem do lasu na grzyby.
Michał: Na grzyby? I co, znaleźliście coś?
Ewa: Tak, cały koszyk! Wieczorem zrobiłam zupę grzybową.
Michał: Super! Szkoda, że nie znam się na grzybach.
Ewa: To następnym razem pojedziesz z nami. Wszystko ci pokażę.
translation:
Ewa: Hi, Michał! How was your weekend?
Michał: Good, thanks. On Saturday I was at the swimming pool with the kids, and on Sunday we went to Grandma's. And you? What did you do?
Ewa: On Saturday I cleaned the flat. On Sunday morning my husband and I went to the forest to pick mushrooms.
Michał: Mushroom picking? And did you find anything?
Ewa: Yes, a whole basket! In the evening I made mushroom soup.
Michał: Great! It's a pity I don't know much about mushrooms.
Ewa: Then next time you'll come with us. I'll show you everything.

questions.q: What are Ewa and Michał talking about?
options: A weekend trip they took together
A weekend course about mushrooms
How each of them spent the weekend
Their plans for the next weekend
questions.explain: Ewa asks 'Jak minął weekend?', and then each of them says what they did on Saturday and on Sunday.

questions.q: What did Michał do on Saturday?
options: He took his children to the pool.
He went to the forest with Ewa.
He went to see Grandma.
He cleaned his flat all day.
questions.explain: Michał says 'W sobotę byłem z dziećmi na basenie'.

questions.q: Ewa says 'Tak, cały koszyk!' What does she mean?
options: They lost their basket in the forest.
They bought a basket of mushrooms.
They found only a few mushrooms.
They found a lot of mushrooms.
questions.explain: Michał asks 'znaleźliście coś?', and Ewa answers that they found a whole basket ('cały koszyk'), so they found a lot.

title: Sylwester u Oli
text:
Ola: Hej! Co robisz w Sylwestra?
Bartek: Jeszcze nie wiem. W zeszłym roku byłem na koncercie w centrum, ale było bardzo zimno i tłoczno. A ty?
Ola: Robię imprezę u siebie. Przyjdziesz? Będzie dziesięć osób.
Bartek: Chętnie! Co mam przynieść?
Ola: Może sałatkę? Ja zrobię bigos, a Kuba przyniesie ciasto.
Bartek: Dobrze, zrobię sałatkę jarzynową. O której zaczynacie?
Ola: Koło dziewiątej. O północy wyjdziemy na balkon. Z dziesiątego piętra widać fajerwerki nad całym miastem!
Bartek: Super! To do zobaczenia trzydziestego pierwszego!
translation:
Ola: Hi! What are you doing on New Year's Eve?
Bartek: I don't know yet. Last year I was at a concert in the city centre, but it was very cold and crowded. And you?
Ola: I'm having a party at my place. Will you come? There will be ten people.
Bartek: I'd love to! What should I bring?
Ola: Maybe a salad? I'll make bigos, and Kuba will bring a cake.
Bartek: OK, I'll make a vegetable salad. What time are you starting?
Ola: Around nine. At midnight we'll go out onto the balcony. From the tenth floor you can see fireworks over the whole city!
Bartek: Great! See you on the thirty-first, then!

questions.q: Why does Ola write to Bartek?
options: To ask him to a concert in the city
To invite him to her New Year's party
To ask him to help her cook bigos
To invite him to her birthday party
questions.explain: Ola asks 'Co robisz w Sylwestra?' and then writes 'Robię imprezę u siebie. Przyjdziesz?'

questions.q: What time does the party start?
options: At midnight
Around ten
Around eight
Around nine
questions.explain: Ola writes 'Koło dziewiątej' (around nine); midnight is when they will go out onto the balcony.

questions.q: Bartek writes 'Chętnie!' What does he mean?
options: He'd be happy to come.
He can't come this time.
He isn't sure yet.
He'll come a bit later.
questions.explain: Ola asks 'Przyjdziesz?', and Bartek answers 'Chętnie!' and then asks what to bring, so he is glad to come.

title: Spacery z psem
text:
SZUKAM OSOBY DO SPACERÓW Z PSEM
W zeszłym tygodniu złamałam nogę. Przez miesiąc muszę siedzieć w domu, a mój pies Bruno potrzebuje długich spacerów.

Szukam pomocy od poniedziałku do piątku. Spacery są rano o 7:00 i wieczorem o 18:00. W weekendy pomaga mi syn.
Bruno ma pięć lat. Jest duży, ale spokojny i grzeczny. Lubi dzieci i inne psy.
Mieszkamy na Żoliborzu, blisko parku.

Płacę 35 zł za spacer.
Tel. 501 234 567, Teresa
translation:
LOOKING FOR SOMEONE TO WALK MY DOG
Last week I broke my leg. For a month I have to stay at home, and my dog Bruno needs long walks.

I'm looking for help from Monday to Friday. The walks are in the morning at 7:00 and in the evening at 18:00. At weekends my son helps me.
Bruno is five years old. He's big, but calm and well-behaved. He likes children and other dogs.
We live in Żoliborz, near a park.

I pay 35 zł per walk.
Tel. 501 234 567, Teresa

questions.q: What is the advert for?
options: To find someone to walk her dog
To offer to walk other people's dogs
To find a home for her dog for a month
To find people to walk her dog for free
questions.explain: The heading says 'SZUKAM OSOBY DO SPACERÓW Z PSEM', and Teresa pays '35 zł za spacer'.

questions.q: What happened to Teresa last week?
options: She broke her arm.
Her son broke his leg.
She broke her leg.
Bruno hurt his leg.
questions.explain: Teresa writes 'W zeszłym tygodniu złamałam nogę' (last week I broke my leg).

questions.q: Who could help Teresa with Bruno?
options: A student who is free only at weekends
A woman who is free at 7:00 and 18:00
A man who is afraid of big dogs
A boy who is free only at lunchtime
questions.explain: Teresa needs help 'od poniedziałku do piątku' at 7:00 and 18:00; at weekends her son helps, and Bruno is big.

title: Przeprowadzka
text:
W sobotę Agata i Adam przeprowadzali się do nowego mieszkania na Pradze. Mieli dużo rzeczy: kanapę, szafę, łóżko i trzydzieści kartonów. Mieszkanie było na czwartym piętrze, ale winda nie działała.

Adam zadzwonił do kolegów i po godzinie przyjechali Tomek i Wojtek. Razem wnosili wszystko po schodach aż do wieczora. Byli bardzo zmęczeni.

Wtedy przyszedł sąsiad i powiedział: „Dobry wieczór! Winda już działa. Pan z serwisu właśnie ją naprawił”. Wszyscy zaczęli się śmiać, a Agata zamówiła dla wszystkich pizzę.
translation:
On Saturday Agata and Adam were moving to a new flat in Praga. They had a lot of things: a sofa, a wardrobe, a bed and thirty boxes. The flat was on the fourth floor, but the lift wasn't working.

Adam called his friends, and an hour later Tomek and Wojtek arrived. Together they carried everything up the stairs until the evening. They were very tired.

Then a neighbour came and said, “Good evening! The lift is working now. The repairman has just fixed it.” Everyone started laughing, and Agata ordered pizza for everyone.

questions.q: What is the story about?
options: A day of painting a new flat
A party for friends in a new flat
Buying furniture for a new flat
A hard day moving into a new flat
questions.explain: Agata and Adam 'przeprowadzali się do nowego mieszkania', and the story follows their long, tiring day.

questions.q: Who helped Agata and Adam?
options: Their new neighbour
Two of Adam's friends
Two men from a company
Agata's two brothers
questions.explain: Adam 'zadzwonił do kolegów', and 'po godzinie przyjechali Tomek i Wojtek'.

questions.q: Why did everyone start laughing?
options: The pizza came very quickly.
The sofa didn't fit through the door.
The lift was working again.
The neighbour was an old friend.
questions.explain: They carried everything up the stairs until the evening, and only then did the neighbour say 'Winda już działa'.

title: Gdzie jest mój kot?
text:
Kasia: Dzień dobry! Czy ktoś widział mojego kota? Jest rudy i ma białe łapki. Wczoraj wieczorem wyszedł na klatkę i nie wrócił.
Pan Henryk: Dzień dobry. Rano słyszałem miauczenie w piwnicy. Może to on?
Kasia: Dziękuję! Już tam idę.
Pani Ela: Piwnica jest zamknięta na klucz. Mam klucz, zaraz zejdę.
Kasia: Jest!!! Siedział za starym rowerem. Był głodny i brudny, ale jest zdrowy.
Pani Ela: Pewnie wszedł tam, kiedy ktoś otworzył drzwi.
Kasia: Bardzo dziękuję wszystkim! Od dziś będę bardziej uważać!
translation:
Kasia: Good morning! Has anyone seen my cat? He's ginger and has white paws. Yesterday evening he went out onto the staircase and didn't come back.
Mr Henryk: Good morning. This morning I heard meowing in the cellar. Maybe it's him?
Kasia: Thank you! I'm going there now.
Mrs Ela: The cellar is locked. I have the key, I'll come down in a minute.
Kasia: He's here!!! He was sitting behind an old bike. He was hungry and dirty, but he's fine.
Mrs Ela: He probably got in there when someone opened the door.
Kasia: Thank you all so much! From now on I'll be more careful!

questions.q: Why does Kasia start the chat?
options: Her cat went out and didn't come back.
She found a cat and is looking for its owner.
She is looking for someone to feed her cat.
She wants to complain about a noisy cat.
questions.explain: Kasia asks 'Czy ktoś widział mojego kota?' and writes that he 'nie wrócił' (didn't come back).

questions.q: Where was the cat?
options: Under a box in the cellar
Under the stairs by the front door
On Mrs Ela's balcony
Behind an old bike in the cellar
questions.explain: Mr Henryk heard meowing 'w piwnicy', and Kasia writes 'Siedział za starym rowerem'.

questions.q: Mrs Ela writes 'zaraz zejdę'. What does she mean?
options: I'll call you in a minute.
I'll leave the key at your door.
I'll come down in a minute.
I'll go and look for the key.
questions.explain: The cellar is locked and Mrs Ela has the key, so 'zaraz zejdę' means she will come down there in a moment.

title: U fryzjera
text:
Fryzjerka: Dzień dobry! Pan był umówiony na dziesiątą?
Piotr: Dzień dobry. Tak, Piotr Marczak.
Fryzjerka: Zapraszam. Jak strzyżemy?
Piotr: Krótko, ale nie za krótko. W sobotę mam wesele siostry i chcę dobrze wyglądać.
Fryzjerka: Rozumiem. Po bokach krócej, a na górze trochę dłużej?
Piotr: Tak, dokładnie. Ostatnio fryzjer obciął mi za dużo i przez miesiąc chodziłem w czapce!
Fryzjerka: Spokojnie, będę uważać… Gotowe. Podoba się panu?
Piotr: Bardzo! Siostra na pewno będzie zadowolona. Ile płacę?
Fryzjerka: Siedemdziesiąt złotych.
Piotr: Proszę. Dziękuję!
translation:
Hairdresser: Good morning! Did you have an appointment for ten?
Piotr: Good morning. Yes, Piotr Marczak.
Hairdresser: Come in. How would you like it cut?
Piotr: Short, but not too short. On Saturday it's my sister's wedding, and I want to look good.
Hairdresser: I see. Shorter on the sides and a bit longer on top?
Piotr: Yes, exactly. Last time the hairdresser cut off too much, and I went around in a hat for a month!
Hairdresser: Don't worry, I'll be careful… Done. Do you like it?
Piotr: Very much! My sister will definitely be pleased. How much is it?
Hairdresser: Seventy złoty.
Piotr: Here you are. Thank you!

questions.q: What happens in the dialogue?
options: A man gets a haircut for his own wedding
A man takes his son for his first haircut
A man asks for a job at a hairdresser's
A man gets a haircut before a family wedding
questions.explain: Piotr has an appointment ('Pan był umówiony na dziesiątą?'), and he says 'W sobotę mam wesele siostry'.

questions.q: How does Piotr want his hair?
options: Shorter on the sides, longer on top
Very short on the sides and on top
Longer on the sides, shorter on top
Long, with only the ends cut
questions.explain: The hairdresser asks 'Po bokach krócej, a na górze trochę dłużej?', and Piotr answers 'Tak, dokładnie'.

questions.q: Why did Piotr wear a hat for a month?
options: It was very cold that month.
His last haircut was too short.
He didn't like his hair colour.
He had no time for a haircut.
questions.explain: Piotr says 'Ostatnio fryzjer obciął mi za dużo' (last time the hairdresser cut off too much), so he hid his short hair under a hat.

title: Pozdrowienia z Warszawy
text:
Temat: Pozdrowienia z Warszawy
Cześć, Lena!
Dziękuję za maila i zdjęcia z Wiednia. Są piękne! U mnie wszystko dobrze. Od września pracuję w nowej firmie i jestem bardzo zadowolona.

Mam pomysł: przyjedź do mnie w czerwcu! Mam teraz większe mieszkanie, więc możesz spać w pokoju gościnnym. Pokażę ci Stare Miasto i Łazienki Królewskie. W niedziele latem są tam koncerty muzyki Chopina pod gołym niebem. Wieczorem zjemy pierogi w mojej ulubionej restauracji.

Napisz, kiedy masz urlop!
Ściskam
Marta
translation:
Subject: Greetings from Warsaw
Hi Lena!
Thanks for your email and the photos from Vienna. They're beautiful! Everything is fine here. Since September I've been working at a new company, and I'm very happy.

I have an idea: come and visit me in June! I have a bigger flat now, so you can sleep in the guest room. I'll show you the Old Town and Łazienki Park. On Sundays in summer there are open-air Chopin concerts there. In the evening we'll eat pierogi at my favourite restaurant.

Write and tell me when you have time off!
Hugs,
Marta

questions.q: Why does Marta write to Lena?
options: To plan a holiday together in Vienna
To say she is moving to a bigger flat
To invite Lena to stay with her
To ask Lena to find her a new job
questions.explain: Marta writes 'Mam pomysł: przyjedź do mnie w czerwcu!' and says Lena can sleep in the guest room.

questions.q: What does Marta say about her job?
options: She started it in June.
She is very happy with it.
She wants to find a new one.
It is too far from home.
questions.explain: Marta writes 'Od września pracuję w nowej firmie i jestem bardzo zadowolona'.

questions.q: Marta writes 'Napisz, kiedy masz urlop!' What does she want to know?
options: When Lena has time off work
When Lena's birthday is
When Lena is moving house
When Lena finishes her course
questions.explain: Marta wants Lena to come in June, so she asks when Lena has her 'urlop': her holiday from work.

title: Zatrzaśnięte drzwi
text:
W piątek wieczorem Paweł wyszedł w kapciach wynieść śmieci. Na schodach usłyszał głośne „bum”: wiatr zatrzasnął drzwi do mieszkania! Klucze i telefon zostały w środku.

Zapasowe klucze miała siostra Pawła, ale mieszkała dwa kilometry dalej. Paweł nie miał pieniędzy na bilet, więc poszedł do niej pieszo. Padał deszcz, a ludzie na ulicy patrzyli na jego kapcie.

Siostra otworzyła drzwi i zaczęła się śmiać. Dała mu klucze, parasol i stare buty męża. Od tej pory Paweł nigdy nie wychodzi z domu bez kluczy.
translation:
On Friday evening Paweł went out in his slippers to take out the rubbish. On the stairs he heard a loud ‘bang’: the wind had slammed the door of his flat shut! His keys and phone were left inside.

Paweł's sister had spare keys, but she lived two kilometres away. Paweł had no money for a ticket, so he walked to her place. It was raining, and people in the street looked at his slippers.

His sister opened the door and started laughing. She gave him the keys, an umbrella and her husband's old shoes. Since then Paweł has never left home without his keys.

questions.q: What is the story about?
options: Paweł loses his keys in the street
Paweł can't get into his flat
Paweł visits his sister for dinner
Paweł forgets his phone at work
questions.explain: The wind 'zatrzasnął drzwi do mieszkania', and Paweł's keys and phone 'zostały w środku'.

questions.q: Why did Paweł walk to his sister's?
options: The trams weren't running.
He wanted some fresh air.
He had no money for a ticket.
He likes walking in the rain.
questions.explain: The text says 'Paweł nie miał pieniędzy na bilet, więc poszedł do niej pieszo'.

questions.q: The text says 'Zapasowe klucze miała siostra Pawła'. What kind of keys did she have?
options: Keys to her own flat
Keys to her husband's car
Old keys that don't work
Extra keys to Paweł's flat
questions.explain: Paweł couldn't get into his flat, and his sister 'Dała mu klucze', so she had a second set of keys to his flat.

title: Prezent dla Moniki
text:
Marek: Cześć! W przyszły czwartek Monika ma urodziny. Kupimy jej coś razem?
Iza: Dobry pomysł! Może przewodnik po Portugalii? W maju tam jedzie.
Jacek: Przewodnik to trochę mało. Proponuję kurs gotowania. Monika uwielbia gotować.
Iza: O, to lepsze! Ile kosztuje?
Jacek: Trzysta złotych. Jest nas sześć osób, więc wychodzi po pięćdziesiąt złotych.
Marek: OK. Przelejcie mi pieniądze na telefon do piątku.
Iza: A kto kupi tort?
Marek: Ja! W czwartek o dziesiątej zrobimy jej niespodziankę w kuchni. Tylko cicho!
translation:
Marek: Hi! Next Thursday is Monika's birthday. Shall we buy her something together?
Iza: Good idea! Maybe a guidebook to Portugal? She's going there in May.
Jacek: A guidebook is a bit too little. I suggest a cooking course. Monika loves cooking.
Iza: Oh, that's better! How much is it?
Jacek: Three hundred złoty. There are six of us, so it comes to fifty złoty each.
Marek: OK. Send me the money by phone transfer by Friday.
Iza: And who will buy the cake?
Marek: Me! On Thursday at ten we'll give her a surprise in the kitchen. Keep it quiet!

questions.q: What are Marek, Iza and Jacek planning?
options: A going-away party for Monika
A cooking course for the whole team
A trip to Portugal in May
A present and a surprise for Monika
questions.explain: Marek writes that Monika 'ma urodziny' and asks 'Kupimy jej coś razem?', and at the end he plans a 'niespodziankę'.

questions.q: Who will buy the cake?
options: Iza
Jacek
Marek
Monika
questions.explain: Iza asks 'A kto kupi tort?', and Marek answers 'Ja!'.

questions.q: Jacek writes 'wychodzi po pięćdziesiąt złotych'. What does he mean?
options: Each person pays 50 zł.
The course costs 50 zł.
They need 50 zł more.
The cake costs 50 zł.
questions.explain: The course costs 'Trzysta złotych' and 'Jest nas sześć osób', so each of the six people pays fifty złoty.

title: Mój pierwszy bieg
text:
Niedziela, 20 września
Dzisiaj był mój pierwszy bieg na dziesięć kilometrów! Trenowałam od marca, trzy razy w tygodniu, na Polu Mokotowskim. Rano byłam bardzo zdenerwowana i prawie nic nie zjadłam.

Pierwsze pięć kilometrów było łatwe, ale potem zrobiło się gorąco i zaczęły mnie boleć nogi. Na ósmym kilometrze chciałam się zatrzymać. Wtedy usłyszałam, jak moja siostra krzyczy: „Dawaj, Julka!” Dobiegłam do mety po godzinie i dwóch minutach.

Jestem zmęczona, ale bardzo szczęśliwa. W przyszłym roku spróbuję przebiec półmaraton!
translation:
Sunday, 20 September
Today was my first ten-kilometre race! I'd been training since March, three times a week, in Pole Mokotowskie park. In the morning I was very nervous and ate almost nothing.

The first five kilometres were easy, but then it got hot and my legs started to hurt. At the eighth kilometre I wanted to stop. Then I heard my sister shouting, “Come on, Julka!” I reached the finish line after one hour and two minutes.

I'm tired but very happy. Next year I'll try to run a half marathon!

questions.q: What is the diary entry about?
options: Julka's first 10 km race
Julka's first day of training
Her sister's first race
A race Julka couldn't finish
questions.explain: Julka writes 'Dzisiaj był mój pierwszy bieg na dziesięć kilometrów!'

questions.q: Where did Julka train?
options: In Łazienki Park
At Pole Mokotowskie
Along the Vistula
At a sports stadium
questions.explain: She writes 'Trenowałam od marca, trzy razy w tygodniu, na Polu Mokotowskim'.

questions.q: Her sister shouted 'Dawaj, Julka!' Why?
options: She wanted Julka to give her water.
She wanted Julka to stop running.
She wanted to give Julka a present.
She wanted Julka to keep going.
questions.explain: Julka writes 'Na ósmym kilometrze chciałam się zatrzymać', and just then her sister shouted 'Dawaj, Julka!' to cheer her on.

title: Pierwszy śnieg
text:
W nocy spadł pierwszy śnieg. Rano pan Robert chciał pojechać do pracy samochodem, jak zawsze. Ale samochód był cały w śniegu i nie chciał zapalić. Robert próbował kilka razy, a potem poszedł na przystanek.

Tramwaj był pełny, ale jechał szybko, bo tramwaje mają własne tory. Samochody na ulicach stały w korkach. Robert był w biurze piętnaście minut wcześniej niż zwykle. Koledzy, którzy przyjechali samochodami, spóźnili się prawie o godzinę.

„Od jutra jeżdżę do pracy tramwajem” – powiedział Robert.
translation:
In the night the first snow fell. In the morning Mr Robert wanted to drive to work, as always. But the car was all covered in snow and wouldn't start. Robert tried a few times, and then he went to the tram stop.

The tram was full, but it went fast, because trams have their own tracks. The cars in the streets were stuck in traffic jams. Robert was at the office fifteen minutes earlier than usual. His colleagues, who came by car, were almost an hour late.

“From tomorrow I'm going to work by tram,” said Robert.

questions.q: What is the main point of the story?
options: Robert was late because of the snow
That day the tram was faster than a car
Robert's colleagues helped with his car
Robert bought a new car after the snow
questions.explain: Robert went by tram and was at work 'piętnaście minut wcześniej niż zwykle', while the cars 'stały w korkach'.

questions.q: Why didn't Robert drive to work?
options: His car wouldn't start.
The roads were closed.
He couldn't find his keys.
His car was at a garage.
questions.explain: The car 'nie chciał zapalić' (wouldn't start), and Robert tried 'kilka razy'.

questions.q: Robert says 'Od jutra jeżdżę do pracy tramwajem'. What does he mean?
options: He'll take the tram only tomorrow.
He'll drive to work again tomorrow.
He'll go by tram every day from now.
He'll buy a tram ticket tomorrow.
questions.explain: 'Od jutra' means 'from tomorrow on': after this morning, Robert has decided to go to work by tram every day.

title: W aptece
text:
Farmaceutka: Dzień dobry. W czym mogę pomóc?
Klient: Dzień dobry. Mam e-receptę na lek na ciśnienie.
Farmaceutka: Dobrze. Poproszę kod z SMS-a i numer PESEL.
Klient: Kod to 4815, a PESEL mam w dowodzie. Proszę.
Farmaceutka: Na recepcie są dwa opakowania, ale mam tylko jedno. Drugie zamówię na jutro.
Klient: Jutro rano wyjeżdżam do córki na tydzień.
Farmaceutka: Nie szkodzi. Jedno weźmie pan teraz, a drugie kupi pan u nas po powrocie.
Klient: Dobrze. Ile płacę?
Farmaceutka: Osiemnaście złotych.
translation:
Pharmacist: Good morning. How can I help you?
Customer: Good morning. I have an e-prescription for blood pressure medicine.
Pharmacist: All right. The code from the text message and your PESEL number, please.
Customer: The code is 4815, and my PESEL number is on my ID card. Here you are.
Pharmacist: The prescription is for two boxes, but I only have one. I'll order the second one for tomorrow.
Customer: Tomorrow morning I'm going to my daughter's for a week.
Pharmacist: Never mind. You'll take one now, and you can buy the second one here when you get back.
Customer: All right. How much is it?
Pharmacist: Eighteen złoty.

questions.q: Why is the man at the pharmacy?
options: To buy medicine for his daughter's trip
To buy something for a cough and a cold
To get his medicine with an e-prescription
To give back medicine he doesn't need
questions.explain: The man says 'Mam e-receptę na lek na ciśnienie' (I have an e-prescription for blood pressure medicine).

questions.q: What does the pharmacist need from him?
options: The doctor's name and his address
A paper prescription from the doctor
His phone and his date of birth
The code from an SMS and his PESEL
questions.explain: She says 'Poproszę kod z SMS-a i numer PESEL'.

questions.q: The man says 'Jutro rano wyjeżdżam do córki na tydzień.' Why does he say this?
options: He wants medicine for his daughter.
He can't come back for it tomorrow.
He wants to pay for it next week.
He wants the pharmacist to hurry.
questions.explain: The pharmacist says 'Drugie zamówię na jutro', but he is leaving tomorrow morning, so he can't come for it then.

title: Problem z ogrzewaniem
text:
Temat: Problem z ogrzewaniem
Dzień dobry, Panie Andrzeju,
piszę, bo od poniedziałku w sypialni jest bardzo zimno. Kaloryfer w tym pokoju jest zimny, chociaż w kuchni i w salonie kaloryfery są ciepłe. Wczoraj próbowałam go mocniej odkręcić, ale to nie pomogło.

Czy mógłby Pan przysłać hydraulika? Jestem w domu codziennie po szesnastej, a w sobotę cały dzień. Śpię teraz na kanapie w salonie, więc proszę o szybką pomoc.

Z góry dziękuję i pozdrawiam
Natalia Wójcik
translation:
Subject: A problem with the heating
Hello Mr Andrzej,
I'm writing because since Monday it has been very cold in the bedroom. The radiator in this room is cold, although the radiators in the kitchen and the living room are warm. Yesterday I tried to turn it up more, but it didn't help.

Could you send a plumber? I'm at home every day after four p.m., and all day on Saturday. I'm sleeping on the sofa in the living room now, so I'm asking for quick help.

Thank you in advance, and best regards,
Natalia Wójcik

questions.q: Why does Natalia write to Mr Andrzej?
options: To ask him to turn on the heating in the building
To ask if she can buy a new radiator
To ask for help with a radiator
To tell him she has fixed a radiator
questions.explain: Natalia describes a problem with a radiator and asks 'Czy mógłby Pan przysłać hydraulika?'

questions.q: When is Natalia at home?
options: Every morning and on Sunday
Only on Saturday morning
Every day before four o'clock
After four, or all day Saturday
questions.explain: She writes 'Jestem w domu codziennie po szesnastej, a w sobotę cały dzień'.

questions.q: Why is Natalia sleeping on the sofa?
options: Her bedroom is too cold.
Her bedroom radiator is leaking.
Her bedroom radiator is too noisy.
A friend is staying with her.
questions.explain: The bedroom radiator is cold, but 'w salonie kaloryfery są ciepłe', so she sleeps in the warm living room.

topic: concert tickets for the wrong date
title: Bilety na koncert
text:
Magda uwielbia jazz. Na jej trzydzieste urodziny Szymon kupił dwa bilety na koncert jej ulubionego pianisty. To miała być niespodzianka.

W dniu urodzin Magda założyła nową sukienkę, a Szymon garnitur. Przyjechali taksówką pół godziny przed koncertem. Przy wejściu pani sprawdziła bilety i powiedziała: „Przykro mi, ale ten koncert jest dwunastego grudnia, a dzisiaj jest dwunasty listopada”. Szymon zrobił się czerwony. Pomylił miesiące!

Ale Magda tylko się roześmiała. Poszli na kolację do restauracji, a miesiąc później jeszcze raz świętowali jej urodziny – na koncercie.
translation:
Magda loves jazz. For her thirtieth birthday Szymon bought two tickets for a concert by her favourite pianist. It was meant to be a surprise.

On her birthday Magda put on a new dress, and Szymon a suit. They arrived by taxi half an hour before the concert. At the entrance a woman checked the tickets and said, “I'm sorry, but this concert is on the twelfth of December, and today is the twelfth of November.” Szymon turned red. He had mixed up the months!

But Magda just laughed. They went out to dinner at a restaurant, and a month later they celebrated her birthday once more – at the concert.

questions.q: What is the story about?
options: A concert that was cancelled at the last minute
A birthday surprise that went a bit wrong
Lost tickets for a birthday concert
A birthday dinner at a jazz club
questions.explain: Szymon planned a birthday surprise ('To miała być niespodzianka'), but at the entrance something went wrong.

questions.q: What was the problem with the tickets?
options: They were for next month.
They were for another city.
They were for last month.
They were only for one person.
questions.explain: The woman says 'ten koncert jest dwunastego grudnia, a dzisiaj jest dwunasty listopada'.

questions.q: Szymon 'zrobił się czerwony'. Why?
options: He was angry with her.
He was hot in his suit.
He felt ill in the taxi.
He felt embarrassed.
questions.explain: Right after this the text says 'Pomylił miesiące!': he had made a silly mistake, so he was embarrassed.

title: Zepsuty czajnik
text:
Klient: Dzień dobry. Tydzień temu kupiłem u państwa ten czajnik, a wczoraj przestał działać.
Sprzedawczyni: Przykro mi. Ma pan paragon?
Klient: Tak, proszę.
Sprzedawczyni: Możemy wysłać czajnik do naprawy, ale to potrwa dwa tygodnie. Albo od razu wymienimy go na nowy.
Klient: Wolę nowy. Bez czajnika nie wytrzymam dwóch tygodni – piję pięć herbat dziennie!
Sprzedawczyni: Rozumiem. Niestety, tego modelu już nie mamy. Mamy podobny, czerwony, ale droższy o trzydzieści złotych.
Klient: Czerwony nie pasuje do mojej kuchni… Ale dobrze, dopłacę.
translation:
Customer: Good morning. A week ago I bought this kettle here, and yesterday it stopped working.
Shop assistant: I'm sorry. Do you have the receipt?
Customer: Yes, here you are.
Shop assistant: We can send the kettle for repair, but it will take two weeks. Or we can exchange it for a new one straight away.
Customer: I'd prefer a new one. I can't last two weeks without a kettle – I drink five cups of tea a day!
Shop assistant: I understand. Unfortunately, we don't have this model any more. We have a similar one, a red one, but it's thirty złoty more expensive.
Customer: Red doesn't go with my kitchen… But all right, I'll pay the difference.

questions.q: Why did the man come back to the shop?
options: He wanted the kettle in another colour
His new kettle stopped working
He paid too much for his kettle
He wanted to buy a second kettle
questions.explain: He says 'Tydzień temu kupiłem u państwa ten czajnik, a wczoraj przestał działać'.

questions.q: Why does he want a new kettle at once?
options: He has guests tonight.
The repair costs too much.
He drinks a lot of tea.
He's moving house soon.
questions.explain: He says he can't wait two weeks without a kettle: 'piję pięć herbat dziennie!'

questions.q: The man says 'dopłacę'. What does he mean?
options: He will pay the difference.
He wants his money back.
He will pay for it later.
He wants a lower price.
questions.explain: The new kettle is 'droższy o trzydzieści złotych', and he agrees to take it, so 'dopłacę' means he will pay the extra thirty złoty.

title: Ważna informacja dla mieszkańców
text:
OGŁOSZENIE
Szanowni Mieszkańcy!
Informujemy, że od 6 lipca (godz. 8:00) do 9 lipca (godz. 18:00) w naszym budynku nie będzie ciepłej wody. W tym czasie robotnicy wymienią stare rury w piwnicy. Zimna woda będzie przez cały czas.

Po naprawie woda z kranu może mieć brązowy kolor. Nie trzeba się tym martwić. Wystarczy odkręcić kran i poczekać kilka minut, aż woda będzie czysta.

Za utrudnienia przepraszamy. W razie pytań prosimy dzwonić pod numer 22 123 45 67.
Administracja budynku
translation:
NOTICE
Dear Residents!
We would like to inform you that from 6 July (8:00) to 9 July (18:00) there will be no hot water in our building. During this time workers will replace old pipes in the cellar. There will be cold water the whole time.

After the repair, the water from the tap may be brown. There is no need to worry about it. Just turn on the tap and wait a few minutes until the water is clean.

We apologise for the inconvenience. If you have any questions, please call 22 123 45 67.
Building management

questions.q: What is the notice about?
options: No cold water for a few days
A new price for hot water
New water meters in all flats
No hot water for a few days
questions.explain: The notice says 'w naszym budynku nie będzie ciepłej wody' from 6 to 9 July.

questions.q: What will the workers do?
options: Clean the water tanks on the roof
Paint the walls in the cellar
Change old pipes in the cellar
Check the water in every flat
questions.explain: The notice says 'robotnicy wymienią stare rury w piwnicy'.

questions.q: On 10 July the water from your tap is brown. What should you do?
options: Turn off the water in the flat
Let the water run for a few minutes
Boil the water before drinking it
Buy bottled water for a few days
questions.explain: The notice says 'Wystarczy odkręcić kran i poczekać kilka minut, aż woda będzie czysta'.

title: Jak segregujemy śmieci?
text:
JAK SEGREGUJEMY ŚMIECI?
Drodzy Sąsiedzi! Przy naszym budynku stoi pięć pojemników na śmieci:
NIEBIESKI – papier: gazety, kartony, zeszyty.
ŻÓŁTY – plastik i metal: butelki, puszki, kartony po mleku i sokach.
ZIELONY – szkło: butelki i słoiki bez nakrętek.
BRĄZOWY – odpady bio: obierki z owoców i warzyw, fusy z kawy, skorupki jajek. Nie wrzucamy tu mięsa ani kości!
CZARNY – wszystko, czego nie można wrzucić do innych pojemników.

Stare meble zostawiamy przy pojemnikach tylko w ostatni piątek miesiąca.
Dziękujemy, że segregujecie!
translation:
HOW DO WE SORT OUR RUBBISH?
Dear Neighbours! There are five rubbish bins by our building:
BLUE – paper: newspapers, cardboard boxes, notebooks.
YELLOW – plastic and metal: bottles, cans, milk and juice cartons.
GREEN – glass: bottles and jars without lids.
BROWN – bio waste: fruit and vegetable peelings, coffee grounds, eggshells. We don't put meat or bones here!
BLACK – everything that can't go into the other bins.

We leave old furniture by the bins only on the last Friday of the month.
Thank you for sorting your rubbish!

questions.q: What is the main purpose of this text?
options: To say the bins will change colour
To ask residents to pay for new bins
To ask for help cleaning the bins
To explain which bin to use for what
questions.explain: Under the heading 'JAK SEGREGUJEMY ŚMIECI?' the text lists five bins and says what goes into each one.

questions.q: Where should you put an empty milk carton?
options: In the yellow bin
In the blue bin
In the green bin
In the black bin
questions.explain: The yellow bin is for 'kartony po mleku i sokach'.

questions.q: After dinner you have some chicken bones. Where do they go?
options: In the brown bin
In the yellow bin
In the black bin
Next to the bins
questions.explain: The brown bin says 'Nie wrzucamy tu mięsa ani kości!', so bones go in the black bin, for 'wszystko, czego nie można wrzucić do innych pojemników'.

topic: first day at a new job
title: Pierwszy dzień w pracy
text:
W poniedziałek Ania zaczynała nową pracę w biurze na Woli. Bała się, że się spóźni, więc wyszła z domu godzinę wcześniej. Przed pracą kupiła jeszcze kawę w kawiarni. Przy wyjściu potknęła się i wylała ją na mężczyznę w białej koszuli. „Bardzo pana przepraszam!” – powiedziała. „Nic się nie stało” – odpowiedział z uśmiechem.

O dziewiątej Ania weszła do biura. Za biurkiem siedział ten sam mężczyzna w koszuli z brązową plamą. „Dzień dobry, jestem Tomasz Nowicki, pani nowy szef. Zapraszam. Tylko dzisiaj bez kawy, dobrze?”
translation:
On Monday Ania was starting a new job at an office in Wola. She was afraid she would be late, so she left home an hour early. Before work she bought a coffee at a café. On the way out she tripped and spilled it on a man in a white shirt. “I'm so sorry!” she said. “No harm done,” he answered with a smile.

At nine Ania walked into the office. Behind the desk sat the same man, in a shirt with a brown stain. “Good morning, I'm Tomasz Nowicki, your new boss. Come in. Only no coffee today, all right?”

questions.q: What is the story about?
options: A funny start to Ania's holiday
Ania's first day working in a café
Ania's interview for a new job
A funny start to Ania's new job
questions.explain: On Monday Ania 'zaczynała nową pracę', and her first morning there didn't go as planned.

questions.q: Who was the man in the café?
options: A waiter in the café
Ania's new boss
Ania's new colleague
Ania's old boss
questions.explain: In the office the same man says 'jestem Tomasz Nowicki, pani nowy szef'.

questions.q: Why does Tomasz say 'Tylko dzisiaj bez kawy, dobrze?'
options: He's joking about the spilt coffee.
Coffee isn't allowed in the office.
The coffee machine is broken.
He thinks coffee is bad for her.
questions.explain: That morning Ania 'wylała ją na mężczyznę w białej koszuli' – on him – so he makes a friendly joke about it.

topic: student asks to move an exam
title: Prośba do pani profesor
text:
Temat: Egzamin z historii sztuki
Szanowna Pani Profesor,
nazywam się Jakub Lis i jestem studentem drugiego roku. Egzamin z historii sztuki odbędzie się 24 czerwca. Niestety, w tym samym dniu biorę udział w zawodach pływackich w Poznaniu. Od początku studiów reprezentuję naszą uczelnię i drużyna bardzo na mnie liczy.

Czy mógłbym zdawać egzamin w innym terminie? W załączniku przesyłam zaświadczenie z klubu sportowego. Mogę przyjść w każdy inny dzień, także w lipcu.

Z wyrazami szacunku
Jakub Lis
translation:
Subject: The history of art exam
Dear Professor,
My name is Jakub Lis, and I'm a second-year student. The history of art exam will take place on 24 June. Unfortunately, on the same day I'm taking part in a swimming competition in Poznań. Since the start of my studies I have represented our university, and the team is really counting on me.

Could I take the exam on a different date? I'm attaching a note from my sports club. I can come on any other day, in July too.

Yours sincerely,
Jakub Lis

questions.q: Why does Jakub write to the professor?
options: To ask about the topics of the exam
To ask if he can take the exam another day
To say he failed the exam because of sport
To invite her to watch a swimming event
questions.explain: Jakub asks 'Czy mógłbym zdawać egzamin w innym terminie?'

questions.q: What does Jakub send with his email?
options: A note from his sports club
A note from his doctor
His swimming results
A ticket for the competition
questions.explain: He writes 'W załączniku przesyłam zaświadczenie z klubu sportowego'.

questions.q: Jakub writes 'drużyna bardzo na mnie liczy'. What does he mean?
options: The team counts his points.
The team pays him to swim.
The team really needs him.
The team is angry with him.
questions.explain: He has represented the university 'Od początku studiów', and this competition is important, so 'na mnie liczy' means the team is counting on him.

title: Dziękuję!
text:
Erik przyjechał ze Szwecji do Warszawy na studia. Polskiego uczył się już od roku i był z siebie bardzo dumny. Pewnego dnia poszedł z kolegą, Filipem, do kawiarni. Rachunek za dwie kawy i szarlotkę wynosił czterdzieści dwa złote. Erik dał kelnerowi sto złotych i grzecznie powiedział: „Dziękuję”. Kelner podziękował z uśmiechem i odszedł. Erik czekał na resztę, ale kelner nie wrócił.

Filip się roześmiał: „Kiedy płacisz i mówisz «dziękuję», kelner myśli, że nie chcesz reszty!” To była najdroższa lekcja polskiego w życiu Erika.
translation:
Erik came from Sweden to Warsaw to study. He had been learning Polish for a year already and was very proud of himself. One day he went to a café with a friend, Filip. The bill for two coffees and an apple cake came to forty-two złoty. Erik gave the waiter a hundred złoty and politely said, “Dziękuję” (Thank you). The waiter thanked him with a smile and walked away. Erik waited for his change, but the waiter didn't come back.

Filip burst out laughing: “When you pay and say ‘dziękuję’, the waiter thinks you don't want any change!” It was the most expensive Polish lesson of Erik's life.

questions.q: What is the story mainly about?
options: An argument with a rude waiter
Erik's first day working in a café
A misunderstanding when Erik pays
Erik's birthday coffee with Filip
questions.explain: Erik says 'Dziękuję' when he pays, and the waiter takes it to mean that he can keep the change, as Filip explains.

questions.q: How much money did Erik give the waiter?
options: 42 zł
100 zł
50 zł
58 zł
questions.explain: The text says 'Erik dał kelnerowi sto złotych'.

questions.q: Erik 'był z siebie bardzo dumny'. What does this mean?
options: He was tired of learning Polish.
He thought Polish was too hard.
He was shy when he spoke Polish.
He was happy with his Polish.
questions.explain: He had been learning Polish 'już od roku' and was pleased with how well he spoke: 'dumny' means proud.
